name: Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul
architect: Noël Coumont and Timothy G. O'Connell
history: French Canadians came to Lewiston in the 1800s to work in the textile mills, and Dominican friars served their parish. Each time the parish divided, its building fund was split too, which delayed the top of the church. It was finished on 18 July 1936 and dedicated on 23 October 1938. It became a basilica in 2004.
arch: A French Gothic Revival granite church with twin towers and a rose window. It was added to the National Register in 1983 as the second-largest church in New England.
features: Its two Casavant Frères pipe organs were both dedicated in 1938.
The gallery organ, with 4,622 pipes, is the largest church organ in Maine.

look.d: The French Gothic rose window honours the French Canadian mill families who built it.
The towers make it one of the landmarks of Lewiston.

fun: Its French name is Basilique Saint-Pierre et Saint-Paul.
journal: Mill workers from Québec built Maine's grandest church. Took two generations.

quiz.q: Which organ is the largest church organ in Maine?
